name: Select Reels
description: A reel editor chooses which conversations from the cut are worth a standalone video, and where each one starts and ends.

inputs.name: audio_spine
inputs.description: State input: audio_spine, when the run has one. Nothing reads it - see input_contract.UNCONSUMED_DECLARATIONS. It is declared because the DAG edge that carries it is what orders this step after the spine, and a routed key with no declaration derives as REQUIRED.

inputs.name: timeline_transcript
inputs.description: What the cut SAYS, per speaker, in timeline time - library/tools/timeline_transcript.py.

inputs.name: creative_direction
inputs.description: The direction this episode is cut under. Read so the step can SAY where the conversation's own measurements contradict it (library/tools/direction_contradiction.py), never to be overridden by it.

inputs.name: creative_brief
inputs.description: The captain's creative direction as markdown, injected by the runner from the project's creative_brief path. Empty when the project declares none. This is where a project says how many reels it wants and what it wants them to be - none of which the engine states.

inputs.name: project_context
inputs.description: The project's context folder plus the learnings routed to this step, as a MAP the model follows with its shell (never a copy). Injected by the runner from the project's context/ folder and learned_context/ store when this step declares it; a stated absence when the project has neither. See library/tools/project_context.py.

inputs.name: brand_constraints
inputs.description: Brand template constraints (injected by the pipeline runner).

inputs.name: video_preferences
inputs.description: The merged video preferences (style.yaml project layer, video.yaml per-video layer - see library/tools/video_prefs). Injected by the runner when the video declares any; absent otherwise. The bridge publishes its SOFT target_length_seconds and content_rules beside the candidates.

outputs.name: reel_candidates
outputs.description: State output: reel_candidates. Built by bridge.py. One row per contiguous exchange stretch the measurements found - the shape of each candidate conversation the model chooses reels from. Empty is the correct answer on a project declaring no speakers - nothing spoken is selected - and on a cut too short to hold a window; it is not a missing measurement.

outputs.name: turns
outputs.description: Bridge output: the STRUCTURE of the conversation - who spoke and between which two seconds - which is what a reader needs to judge whether a stretch is a two-hander. Carries no words: a turn's text is its segments' texts joined, so publishing it would be the summary and the structure it was rendered from (AGENTS.md 10.1). Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: length_guidance_seconds
outputs.description: Bridge output: the brief's length guidance as numbers - published rather than enforced, because a hard ceiling silently withholds every story that needs longer to finish. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: target_length_seconds
outputs.description: Bridge output, only when the project's video preferences declare it: the SOFT target_length_seconds the video is cut toward - guidance the model weighs, never a gate or a refusal. Beside length_guidance_seconds, not replacing it. Declared here because the bridge emits it on such runs and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: target_length_note
outputs.description: Bridge output, with target_length_seconds only: what the soft target is. Declared here because the bridge emits it on such runs and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: content_rules
outputs.description: Bridge output, only when the project's video preferences declare them: content_rules (speakers_must_interact, require_value_add, require_cta) - the project's own statement of what a reel must do. Absence keeps today's format behaviour. Declared here because the bridge emits it on such runs and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: picture_holes
outputs.description: Bridge output: the transcript's measured picture holes, carried beside the candidates so a span is never drawn over seconds with no picture. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: lead_speaker
outputs.description: Bridge output: which speaker asks - the inferred lead of the exchange. Inferred, not declared; the handoff invites correction. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: answering_speaker
outputs.description: Bridge output: the other voice - the speaker the lead is measured against. Absent on the monologue path: a one-speaker project has no second voice, and a null one would read as a missing one. Declared here because the bridge emits it on conversation runs and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: who_leads_was_inferred
outputs.description: Bridge output: WHY the lead/answerer inference was drawn, in numbers - ask rates and mean turn lengths for both voices. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: undetermined
outputs.description: Bridge output: what the model needs told - why no exchange can be identified on the degenerate path (the transcript names fewer than two speakers, and a reel is a conversation), or where the transcript disagrees with the project's declared speaker roster on any other path. (A bridge key, not the could_not_determine demand signal in library/tools/undetermined.py.) Declared here because the bridge emits it on such runs and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: declared_speakers
outputs.description: Bridge output, only when the project declares source.speakers: the roster ([{name, role?}]) the speaker-count thresholds read - monologue, zero, or conversation. [] is a declared-zero project, not an absence. Declared here because the bridge emits it on such runs and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.
